_comment: GOLDEN-305, 30 epoch, DUAL-FREQUENCY + NO SATELLITE OSB ESTIMATION — the speed arm.
Extends the dual probe and adds the single change network.estimate_sat_code_bias: false,
so satellite code biases are APPLIED FROM EXTERNAL PRODUCTS (.BIA) instead of co-estimated.
303 in-network GPS-only, channel_mode single, lane_carry OFF, full golden instrumentation,
WTZZ00DEU closed-loop consumer.  30 epochs at 30 s = 900 s.
PURPOSE: a fast iteration base.  Removing the co-estimated OSB block drops n_cb states and
their gauge rows from the shared block, which is the part of the epoch that scales as
O(shared_dim^2) through cov-consumers and the carry algebra.  Read the D0/D0b section
medians over settled epochs; do NOT read wall, and do NOT compare against any arm that ran
while another 305 job held the box.
BASELINES for the comparison (all 303 sta, GPS-only, lane OFF, same instrumentation):
- _golden305_gps_30m.json      : frequency_mode ALL,  estimate_sat_code_bias TRUE
- _golden305_gps_30ep_dual.json: frequency_mode DUAL, estimate_sat_code_bias TRUE
- THIS ARM                     : frequency_mode DUAL, estimate_sat_code_bias FALSE
Two knobs separate arm 1 from arm 3, so grade the dual step and the OSB step SEPARATELY
against arm 2 in the middle.  Arm 1's measured settled epoch was ~32.6-36 s BUT it ran
concurrently with a sibling 305 job holding roughly half the box; arms 2 and 3 have a
clean machine.  That confound is why the dual-vs-all speed claim must come from arm 2 vs
arm 3 on equal footing, not from arm 1.
WHY estimate_sat_code_bias:false IS LEGITIMATE HERE, not a hack: Odijk et al. 2016
(J Geod 90:15-44) shows the satellite code biases on the first two frequencies are not
separately estimable in the undifferenced/uncombined model — the IF combination of
(d^s_1, d^s_2) is absorbed into the satellite CLOCK and the GF combination into the
IONOSPHERE.  Estimable satellite OSB appears from the THIRD frequency onward.  So a
two-frequency producer that does not co-estimate OSB is the CONFORMANT model, and one
that does is asking a much weaker question of the data.
⚠️ BUT the 2026-08-04 dual probe at 305 sta SOLVED with estimate_sat_code_bias TRUE
(n_cb = 102, 37 gauge rows: IF pin for 32 sats + sum-to-zero for 5 (const,signal) levels),
so the textbook two-frequency counting is NOT what this implementation does: OSB here is
per-(sat, SIGNAL) across multiple tracking attributes and a diverse station set, not two
code observables per satellite.  The 63-station dual arm's failure is therefore more
likely the >=2-STATION admission gate on sparse (sat,signal) columns — its own fatal names
'confirm >= 2 overlapping stations' and points at network.cb_admission — than a pure
frequency-count wall.  Do not repeat the frequency-count explanation without checking
n_cb and the gauge-row count in the log first.
EXPECTED COUNTER CHANGES (verify, do not assume): the prires 'cb' family should go to ZERO
rows with its named WARN (it censuses carried SATELLITE code-bias priors, and there are
none), leaving 'rxcb' as the live family; cb_kaula_prior should report INERT since there
is no CB column to prior; carry_rx_code_bias is a RECEIVER-side knob and stays live.  If
the 'cb' family still shows rows, estimate_sat_code_bias did not actually take effect.
FRESH LINEAGE ONLY.  Own paths; never resume onto another arm's snapshot.
